description: I'm Fahad, who builds software with AI tools. Our team is taking on "Flame in Freefall": an AI-powered dashboard that explains NASA's microgravity combustion research for Moon and Mars fire safety. I'll handle the build and demo. I'm looking for someone with a physics or combustion background, a data/AI person, a designer for clean charts, and a writer for the submission. Beginners are welcome. Send a request and tell me your role.
summary: Flame in Freefall is an independent web dashboard that turns NASA's microgravity combustion research into fire-safety answers for crewed spacecraft, Moon bases and pressurized rovers. You enter oxygen, pressure and airflow (presets: Moon base 30% at 10.2 psi, spacesuit 100% at 4.3 psi), and it ranks 24 NASA PSI investigations by relevance, with a visible formula, confidence and a score breakdown. Every value cites its NASA source; anything NASA did not state is shown as "Not stated", never zero. It also shows what changed between tests, compares investigations, charts where NASA's oxygen and pressure data actually sit against Moon-base conditions, exports 1,500+ test rows for modeling, and answers questions only from the catalog with citations. It is important because the data is hard to find and compare, and the gaps (no partial-gravity data) matter for safe exploration.
details: Ranks 24 NASA PSI combustion investigations against your spacecraft, Moon-base or rover conditions (oxygen, pressure, airflow) with a visible formula and confidence. Presets follow the challenge: Moon base 30% oxygen at 10.2 psi, spacesuit 100% at 4.3 psi. Relevance, not danger. Pages: Matchmaker, Explorer (CSV/JSON), Compare, Gaps (charts of where NASA oxygen and pressure data sit against Moon-base conditions), Ask (answers only from the catalog with cited records), On Earth (NASA Spinoff). Each investigation shows what stayed the same or changed between tests; about 1,500 test rows are downloadable for modeling. Every value cites a NASA source; missing values show as Not stated, never zero. Gaps: oxygen and pressure not stated for SAFFIRE-III, SAME, SAME-R and SLICE; PSI has no partial-gravity data. Tools: Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind, Zod, Python, pandas, pydantic, Vercel; Ask uses Google Gemini with citation checks. Independent project, not endorsed by NASA.
